mainTopic: Wine that turned to vinegar: readings of the ברייתא about checking a barrel for תרומה, the ברכה over wine that smells like vinegar, and who bears the loss when a sold barrel sours.
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a man who checks a barrel of wine so he can keep separating תרומה from it, and later finds it has turned to vinegar. The ברייתא says 'three days are certain, after that is a doubt' but does not say what is certain. רבי יוחנן reads it as: the first three days after the check are definitely wine, because wine sours from the top and a vinegar smell with a wine taste is still wine. רבי יהושע בן לוי reads it as: the last three days before the discovery are definitely vinegar, because souring may start at the bottom, and a vinegar smell with a wine taste already counts as vinegar. The scholars of the South report a three-part version: first days wine, last days vinegar, middle days a doubt. The גמרא asks how that version can be consistent, and answers that it is talking about strong vinegar, which proves real souring three days earlier. רב מרי and רב זביד then disagree over which reading רב יוסף used to decide the ברכה over such wine. Finally, a new topic opens: when a sold barrel turns to vinegar, רב rules that the first three days are the seller's responsibility and after that the buyer's.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a barrel that turned to vinegar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted about someone who checked a barrel of wine in order to keep separating תרומה from it, and later found it had become vinegar. Three days are 'certain' and after that it is a 'doubt'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Someone checks a barrel so he can keep on separating תרומה from it, and afterward it is found to be vinegar. For three days it is certain; from then on it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a source for the discussion. The ברייתא gives a short rule about a barrel of wine that was checked and later found to be vinegar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man checked the barrel so he could keep naming its wine as תרומה for his other wine. Later it turned out to be vinegar, so we need to know when it turned. The ברייתא says 'three days are certain' but does not say certain wine or certain vinegar, or which three days, and that gap drives the rest of the passage.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא)
Separates תרומה (the portion given to a כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says WHAT is certain. Don't assume 'certain' means 'certain wine'. The next two opinions disagree about exactly this.

phrases.english: As it is taught: one who checks the barrel
in order to keep on separating תרומה based on it,
and afterward it was found to be vinegar;
all three days: certain,
from here on: a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא as a source for the discussion that came right before this passage.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's attempt, just before this passage, to settle which ברכה to say over wine that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about checking a barrel before separating תרומה from it.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the unclear ברייתא is actually saying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means. This line sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'three days, certain' are too short to understand alone. The גמרא is not challenging the ruling. It is asking which days are meant and what is certain about them.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which three days the ברייתא means, and whether 'certain' means certain wine or certain vinegar.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the first three days are definitely wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that for the first three days after the check, the barrel is definitely considered wine. After that its status is a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is what it means. The first three days are definitely wine; from then on it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. 'Certain' means the barrel was certainly still wine during the first three days after it was checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן counts forward from the day of the check. Any תרומה separated in those first three days was separated from real wine. After three days we can no longer be sure the wine had not soured, so it becomes a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said, this is what it is saying:
all of the first three days
are definitely wine,
from here on: a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the ברייתא means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first three days after the check are definitely wine; after that it is a ספק.

steps.title: Why the first days are wine: wine sours from the top
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's reasoning: wine starts to sour at the top of the barrel, and that top layer is exactly what the man tasted, and it had not soured.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Wine sours from the top, and this man tasted it and it had not soured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for רבי יוחנן's reading. Since souring begins at the top, and he tasted the top and found good wine, the whole barrel was wine at the time of the check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The check is reliable because it tested the very spot where souring would show up first. If the top was still wine, nothing below it had soured yet. This proves the barrel was wine at the moment of checking.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Wine sours from the top,
and this one tasted it and it had not soured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first three days are treated as definitely wine.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Souring starts at the top, and the top was tasted and found to be wine.

steps.title: Even if it began souring right after the taste, it still counts as wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא handles a possible objection: maybe the wine started to sour right after he tasted it. Even so, at first only the smell turns to vinegar while the taste stays wine, and such wine is still considered wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it started to sour right after he tasted it, it would have the smell of vinegar but the taste of wine, and anything that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine is wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible objection to רבי יוחנן's reasoning. Even if souring began right after the check, the barrel still counts as wine for a while.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the check only shows the barrel was wine at that moment, not for the next three days. The answer is that souring starts with the smell and only later reaches the taste. Since the הלכה follows the taste, wine that only smells like vinegar is still wine.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (introduces a possible objection)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, two facts make the first three days 'definitely wine': souring starts at the top, which was tasted, and early souring changes only the smell, while the taste decides.

phrases.english: If you will say:
right after he tasted it, it soured;
it would have a smell of vinegar and a taste of wine,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל רֵיחֵיהּ חַלָּא וְטַעְמֵיהּ חַמְרָא – חַמְרָא.
phrases.english: and anything whose smell is vinegar and whose taste is wine is wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a possible hole in the reasoning of the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a good taste at the check proves the barrel stayed wine afterward.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wine might have started souring immediately after he tasted it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Even granting the worry, its status in הלכה stays wine because of how souring progresses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once souring begins, the barrel is vinegar.
steps.terutzMaskana: Early souring changes only the smell; with the taste of wine, it is still wine.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the last three days are definitely vinegar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the ברייתא the other way: the three days right before the vinegar was discovered are definitely vinegar, and the days before that, back toward the check, are a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The last three days are definitely vinegar; from then back, it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a different reading of the same ברייתא. He counts backward from the day the vinegar was found, not forward from the day of the check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, 'certain' means certain wine, counted from the check. For רבי יהושע בן לוי, 'certain' means certain vinegar, counted back from the discovery. In his view, תרומה separated in those last three days was separated from vinegar, and the earlier days are a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: From here and beyond (here: going backward in time)

steps.whatToRemember: Same ברייתא, two readings: רבי יוחנן says the first three days after the check are definitely wine; רבי יהושע בן לוי says the last three days before the discovery are definitely vinegar.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions use a similar phrase (מכאן ואילך for רבי יוחנן, מכאן ולהלן for רבי יהושע בן לוי), but they point in opposite directions. For רבי יוחנן it means going forward from the check. For רבי יהושע בן לוי it means going backward from the discovery.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
all of the last three days
are definitely vinegar.
From here and beyond: a doubt.
phrases.notes: Here 'beyond' means going back in time, toward the day he checked the barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a reading of the ברייתא that is the opposite of רבי יוחנן's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three days before the vinegar was discovered are definitely vinegar; the earlier days are a ספק.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two readings disagree on whether תרומה separated in those days was separated from real wine. That decides whether the other wine is properly tithed.

steps.title: Why רבי יהושע בן לוי worries: souring may start at the bottom
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reasons that wine begins to sour from the bottom of the barrel. So the tester, who tasted only the top, could have missed souring that had already begun.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Wine starts to sour from the bottom. So we can say it had already begun to sour, and he simply did not know it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רבי יהושע בן לוי's view in Step 6, that the earlier days are a doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן relied on the idea that souring starts at the top, the part the man actually tasted. רבי יהושע בן לוי says it starts at the bottom, which no one tasted. So a good-tasting top layer proves nothing about the whole barrel, and every day back to the check is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'uprooted'; here it means the wine began to sour

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking for the reason behind רבי יהושע בן לוי's view from the previous step.

phrases.english: Wine begins to sour from the bottom,
so say it had already begun to sour and he was not aware of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading in Step 6, and directly opposes the premise רבי יוחנן used in Step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Souring starts at the bottom of the barrel, which the tester never tasted, so it may already have begun unnoticed.

steps.title: Even if souring starts at the top, a vinegar smell already counts as vinegar
steps.stepSummary: Even if wine sours from the top, it may have started right after he tasted it. Wine that smells like vinegar but still tastes like wine counts as vinegar, so the doubt remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if you say it sours from the top, and he tasted it and it had not soured: perhaps it began to sour right after he tasted it. Then it would smell like vinegar and taste like wine, and something that smells like vinegar and tastes like wine counts as vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהושע בן לוי a second reason. Even if we accept רבי יוחנן's idea that souring starts at the top, his doubt still holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors Step 5 but reaches the opposite result. רבי יוחנן said wine that smells like vinegar and tastes like wine is still wine. רבי יהושע בן לוי says that wine is vinegar, so the moment the smell changes, the barrel's status is already in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (that is, even if you grant this point)
Its smell is vinegar and its taste is wine

steps.confusionAlert: The same phrase, 'smells like vinegar, tastes like wine', appeared in Step 5, where it was ruled wine. Here, in רבי יהושע בן לוי's view, it is ruled vinegar. This is the key point where the two opinions disagree.

phrases.english: And if you say it begins to sour from the top,
and he tasted it and it had not soured,
perhaps after he tasted it, it began to sour.
Then its smell would be vinegar and its taste wine,
and something that smells like vinegar and tastes like wine counts as vinegar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grants רבי יוחנן's premise for argument's sake and shows that רבי יהושע בן לוי's doubt still stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Even granting the other side's premise, a different rule about smell versus taste keeps the doubt alive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If souring starts at the top and the top tasted fine, the barrel should be clearly wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Souring may have begun right after the tasting, and a vinegar smell alone already makes it vinegar.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the real disagreement between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי is about how to classify wine that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine.

steps.title: The דרומאי's three-part version: first days wine, last days vinegar, middle a doubt
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of the South report רבי יהושע בן לוי differently. The first days after the check are definitely wine, the last days before discovery are definitely vinegar, and the days in between are a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Southerners taught in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the first days are definitely wine, the last days are definitely vinegar, and the middle days are a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new version of רבי יהושע בן לוי's opinion is brought. It combines both earlier ideas into a three-part rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version takes רבי יוחנן's 'first three days are wine' and the 'last three days are vinegar' idea, and treats only the stretch in between as a doubt. It sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: The Southerners taught
in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי:
The first days are definitely wine,
phrases.notes: He means the first three days right after the check.

phrases.english: the last days are definitely vinegar,
the middle days are a doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרוֹמָאֵי מַתְנוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different report of רבי יהושע בן לוי's view, which combines the earlier two readings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First three days after the check are definitely wine, last three days before discovery are definitely vinegar, and the middle is a doubt.

steps.title: The three-part version seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The 'first days are wine' rule implies that vinegar smell with wine taste counts as wine. The 'last days are vinegar' rule implies that the same mixture counts as vinegar. Both cannot be true.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement itself is difficult. You said the first days are definitely wine, which shows that something smelling like vinegar but tasting like wine is wine. Then you said the last days are definitely vinegar, which shows that something smelling like vinegar but tasting like wine is vinegar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the דרומאי's version by showing that its two halves seem to rely on opposite rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three days can only be 'definitely wine' if the early stage of souring, where only the smell has changed, still counts as wine. But calling the last three days 'definitely vinegar' seems to count that same early stage as vinegar. So one opinion holds two opposite rules.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)

phrases.english: This statement itself is difficult:
you said the first days are definitely wine,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא רֵיחֵיהּ חַלָּא וְטַעְמֵיהּ חַמְרָא – חַמְרָא;
phrases.english: which shows that something smelling like vinegar but tasting like wine is wine.
And then you said the last days are definitely vinegar,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא רֵיחֵיהּ חַלָּא וְטַעְמֵיהּ חַמְרָא – חַלָּא!
phrases.english: which shows that something smelling like vinegar but tasting like wine is vinegar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the דרומאי's version from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The דרומאי's three-part version of רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each half of the rule implies an opposite ruling about wine that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine.

steps.title: The case is strong vinegar, which needs three days of real souring
steps.stepSummary: The 'last days are vinegar' rule is about a barrel found with strong vinegar. Such vinegar proves it had truly soured, in taste too, at least three days earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where strong vinegar was found. If it had not soured three days earlier, strong vinegar would not have been found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by narrowing the case to one where the vinegar found was strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דרומאי consistently hold that wine that only smells like vinegar is still wine. The last three days are 'definitely vinegar' because strong vinegar can only form after at least three days of full souring. So those days were vinegar in taste too, not just in smell.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; it is a case where

steps.whatToRemember: In the דרומאי's version, wine that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine is still wine. The last three days count as definitely vinegar only because finding strong vinegar proves the taste itself had already turned three days earlier.

phrases.english: It is a case where strong vinegar was found,
for if it had not soured three days before,
strong vinegar would not have been found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 10 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (strong vinegar was found)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Last days are vinegar' seemed to count a mere vinegar smell as vinegar.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strong vinegar proves real souring, in taste too, at least three days earlier, so a vinegar smell alone is still treated as wine.

steps.title: Which explanation did רב יוסף rely on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the explanations of the ברייתא רב יוסף used to settle the ברכה question.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whose explanation did he settle the question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב יוסף, who used this ברייתא to settle which ברכה to say over wine that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine. It asks which of the explanations we just learned he was following, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have now seen different explanations of the ברייתא, and they disagree about whether vinegar smell with wine taste counts as wine or as vinegar. So רב יוסף's proof only works if we know which explanation he held. The answer decides whether the ברכה is בורא פרי הגפן or שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? In line with whose view?
He resolved or settled a question

phrases.english: According to whom did he resolve it?
phrases.notes: "He" is רב יוסף, who used this ברייתא to decide the ברכה over wine that smells like vinegar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanations of the ברייתא are finished, the גמרא returns to רב יוסף's practical use of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which explanation of the ברייתא (רבי יוחנן's or רבי יהושע בן לוי's) רב יוסף relied on to decide the ברכה.

steps.title: רב מרי and רב זביד disagree about רב יוסף's view
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא says רב יוסף followed רבי יוחנן (it counts as wine). The other says he followed רבי יהושע בן לוי (it counts as vinegar).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי and רב זביד disagree about it. One says he followed רבי יוחנן, and the other says he followed רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that two אמוראים disagree about which explanation רב יוסף followed. The question is left without a final decision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב יוסף followed רבי יוחנן, wine that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine counts as wine, so you say בורא פרי הגפן. If he followed רבי יהושע בן לוי, it counts as vinegar, so you say שהכל. The disagreement about the ברייתא turns straight into a disagreement about the ברכה.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה over wine that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine depends on the dispute: following רבי יוחנן it is wine (בורא פרי הגפן), and following רבי יהושע בן לוי it is vinegar (שהכל). The גמרא does not decide between them.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב מָרִי וְרַב זְבִיד;
phrases.english: Rav Mari and Rav Zevid disagree about it;
one said: according to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
phrases.notes: Following רבי יוחנן, the drink counts as wine, so the ברכה is the one for wine.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: and one said: according to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב מָרִי וְרַב זְבִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 by reporting a disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is disputed: one says רב יוסף followed רבי יוחנן (wine), the other says he followed רבי יהושע בן לוי (vinegar).

steps.title: A sold barrel turns to vinegar: the first three days are the seller's responsibility
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. When a sold barrel of wine turns to vinegar, רב rules the seller is responsible during the first three days, and after that the buyer is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone sells a barrel of wine to his friend and it turns to vinegar, רב said: for all of the first three days it is in the seller's responsibility; from then on it is in the buyer's responsibility.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion about buying and selling: who takes the loss when a barrel of wine sours after the sale. רב gives the first opinion, and it is introduced with איתמר, which signals that other אמוראים will disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wine sours within three days, we assume it was already going bad at the seller's, so the sale was faulty and the seller takes the loss. After three days, we assume it soured at the buyer's, so the loss is his.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated; it opens a dispute between אמוראים
In the seller's domain; the seller takes the loss
In the buyer's domain; the buyer takes the loss

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for who takes the loss on spoiled goods after a sale, and the rest of the סוגיא will test and argue with רב's three-day rule.

phrases.english: It was stated: one who sells a barrel of wine to his fellow,
and it turned to vinegar –

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
phrases.english: Rav said: all of the first three days
are in the domain of the seller,
phrases.notes: He means the seller is responsible, because we assume it was already going sour while it was still his.

phrases.english: from here onward, in the domain of the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברכה discussion and opens a new topic: who bears the loss when a sold barrel of wine turns to vinegar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: if a sold barrel sours within the first three days, the seller bears the loss; after that, the buyer does.
